solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nothing thrown skyward in active volcano

indicators.note: in a down clue, something thrown skyward travels upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top
the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something flung up out of the crater of a live volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVE is the tennis score of zero, hence 'Nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, love means a score of zero, so it can stand for nothing.

clue.text: Earth in doormat shifted with steady beating

indicators.note: things shifted are moved about, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for earth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone beats the dust out of a doormat with a steady rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: The earth is put into the doormat's letters and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is the musical direction for a moderate, even tempo, so it describes playing with a steady beat.

clue.text: Chaste person canonised cutting meat

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing goes inside it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: veal is calf meat
a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A holy, celibate figure carving the joint at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestal virgins were the chaste priestesses of Vesta in Rome, so a vestal is a pure, celibate person.

clue.text: Brother of 5 mashed beans, adding in wine

indicators.note: mashed food is crushed out of its shape, so these letters lose their order
adding something in means putting it inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A recipe step: mash the beans and stir in some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is VIOLA; in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night her twin brother is SEBASTIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebastian is Viola's shipwrecked twin brother in Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Sex with Nordic king endless for sister of 22 25

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
Olaf was the name of several Norwegian kings

explanation.surface: A racy saga about a Norse monarch with no ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is not about intimacy at all: it is the Latin number six. 22 25 is TWELFTH NIGHT, whose heroine is Viola.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, twin sister of Sebastian.

clue.text: Absolute nonsense from Yaxley-Lennon?

blocks.note: surface reading: utter rubbish
setter's reading: Stephen Yaxley-Lennon is the English far-right activist known as Tommy Robinson, so his nonsense is his rot

explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Yaxley-Lennon goes by the name Tommy Robinson, so rubbish from him is, punningly, a Tommy's rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot is an informal British word for utter nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Engine conks out on elevated railroad

blocks.note: a machine that conks out stops working
the El is the American name for an elevated railroad, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A locomotive breaks down while running on an overhead railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a compression-ignition engine, or a locomotive powered by one.

clue.text: Bans legend in speaking for Wayland?

indicators.note: in speaking means the word is to be heard, not read, and spelt by its sound

blocks.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it
a legend is a myth

explanation.surface: Someone forbids telling the old tales about a mythical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayland the Smith is the smith-god of Germanic legend; the question mark flags him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayland is the legendary metalworker of Norse and English folklore, an example of a smith who forges iron.

clue.text: Magical land with a certain bracing air

blocks.note: the Land of Oz from The Wizard of Oz
'a certain' person is 'one'

explanation.surface: A fairyland with its own invigorating atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is informal for fresh, invigorating sea air, from the sharp smell once attributed to it.

clue.text: Trade and oil supply stopped by international leader

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
a gap stopped by something is plugged with it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Trade and oil shipments are halted by a world statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun but reads as 'supplely'. 'Leader' is not a statesman but a newspaper's lead article.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is British for a newspaper's lead opinion article, which is also called an editorial.

clue.text: Mycenaean princess to choose Egyptian god

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A Greek princess picks a deity from Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra was the daughter of Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, in Greek myth and tragedy.

clue.text: Greek character, second in charge, strains

blocks.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
S is the abbreviation for second
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A Greek deputy under heavy pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' reads as stress, but here it means melodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Strains are passages of melody, so the plural noun can stand for music.

clue.text: Disreputable yes-man not entirely corrupt

indicators.note: something not entirely there is missing its last part
corrupt text is garbled, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A shady sycophant who is only partly bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamy describes the sordid, unpleasant side of life, hence disreputable.

clue.text: Grassland allowed to cover fine tract

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Meadowland permitted to cover a good stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' suggests an area of land, but here it is a short printed pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, usually on a religious or political subject, as is a leaflet.

clue.text: Gems expert left — beekeeper seizing day

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing it and holding it within

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an apiarist keeps bees
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A jewel specialist walks out while a beekeeper grabs the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapidarist, or lapidary, is a specialist in cutting, engraving and judging precious stones.

clue.text: Luxurious vehicle moves along smoothly

blocks.note: first meaning: a ...-Royce car, informally
second meaning: travels by turning over and over or gliding along

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is one smooth-running car; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls is short for a Rolls-Royce limousine, and rolls is also the verb for gliding along on wheels.

clue.text: Confined prior to Green Street Festival

blocks.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in
eco- means environmentally green
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Locked in ahead of an environmental street party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Street Festival' looks like a single event, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is the Christian feast celebrating the descent of the Holy Spirit, fifty days after Easter.

clue.text: Expert horseman in team, Neo is returning star

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words are read from right to left
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI
the setter Neo speaking of himself says I am
a centaur is a mythical half-man, half-horse

explanation.surface: A skilled rider in the squad, and Neo comes back as a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Neo is' gives I AM; the horseman goes inside that once it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf, the nearest star to the Sun, in the constellation Centaurus.

clue.text: Year's aid distributed: it seems likely

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A twelve-month grant handed out, apparently probably.
explanation.definitionFit: I dare say is a conversational phrase meaning probably, or I suppose so.

clue.text: Lunatic in a fury boxing learner? So hit below belt!

definitions.note: an adverbial description: hitting below the belt is doing it this way

indicators.note: something lunatic is crazy, so these letters are wildly rearranged
boxing something encloses it as in a box

blocks.note: the letters of these words
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A boxer in a rage pummels a novice and lands a low blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' fits the fight scene but is the container signal. Hitting below the belt is a foul in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow below the belt is illegal in boxing, so striking there is fighting in a way that breaks the rules.

clue.text: US lawyer astride sheep in exciting situation

indicators.note: sitting astride something means having it between the legs, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An American attorney riding a sheep would be quite a sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or turbulent event, as in 'what a drama'.

clue.text: Region once densely wooded, forest ultimately burning

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, once thickly wooded
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient woodland district whose forest is finally on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is a historic area of Warwickshire, England, famous as Shakespeare's Forest of Arden.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent comes from Latin for burning and means passionate or fervent, as in burning desire.

clue.text: Glorious day almost here: time for 20 in which 12 be the 28 of 1

blocks.note: the Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, starts the British grouse-shooting season
nigh means near, almost at hand
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The Glorious Twelfth is nearly upon us: time for the shooting season.
explanation.walkthrough: Replacing the numbers gives 'drama in which music be the food of love', the opening line of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy opens with Orsino saying 'If music be the food of love, play on'.

clue.text: Going out for example on steamship

blocks.note: eg is the abbreviation for for example
re means concerning, on the subject of
SS is the prefix for steamship

explanation.surface: Leaving, say, by boarding a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a formal noun for the act of leaving or a way out.

clue.text: Singer's asset managed by vacuous Genoese?

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside is removed and only the outer letters stay

blocks.note: to run something is to manage it
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An opera singer's voice handled by an empty-headed Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer's range is the span of notes their voice can reach, a valuable professional asset.

clue.text: See 22
Hill chain, cooler, at first obscured

indicators.note: with its start hidden from view, the first letter disappears

blocks.note: a fridge is a cooler

explanation.surface: A mountain range, chillier, whose peaks are lost in cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long, narrow line of high ground, a chain of hilltops.

clue.text: City road: upright character in greasy spoon

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed inside the later one

blocks.note: a greasy spoon is a cheap British cafe, a caff
RD is the abbreviation for road
the letter I stands straight up

explanation.surface: A town street where an honest fellow eats at a cheap diner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardiff is the capital of Wales; a caff is British slang for a basic cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Chow, no-good woofer old female raised

indicators.note: with no good means the letter for good is taken away
in a down clue, raised means lifted up, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: a woofer is a barking dog
O is the abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A chow chow, a useless old bitch of a dog, held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chow' looks like the dog breed, which fits 'woofer', but here it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow is informal slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Tries to bronze, but ashen son fails

indicators.note: something that fails falls apart, and the letters collapse into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a tan, but the pale lad does not manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'but' is part of the jumbled letters, not just a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunbathe is to lie in the sun to get a tan, so it is trying to turn one's skin bronze.

clue.text: Saint in Lisbon swallows fifty-five shots

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside

blocks.note: São is the Portuguese word for saint
LV is 55 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Lisbon saint knocks back fifty-five drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' and 'swallows' suggest drinking, but the shots are gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of shots.
